task.title: Persist due recurrence pages through the CLI
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/909 by exposing atomic bounded due-page provenance persistence through a thin deterministic writable CLI adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Validate recurrence identity and page size before writable storage access and require the observed definition revision.
Delegate due selection and all-or-nothing persistence to the kernel and emit complete occurrence-page JSON.
Emit one categorized escaped diagnostic with no stdout and no selected prefix on every failure.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused CLI integration test failed because persist-due was an unrecognized recurrence subcommand.
attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the acceptance contract before adding production behavior.

attempts.diagnostic: Added recurrence persist-due and delegated validated identity, revision, cursor, page size, and cutoff directly to RecurrenceStore::persist_due_occurrences_page.
attempts.patch: Added recurrence persist-due and delegated validated identity, revision, cursor, page size, and cutoff directly to RecurrenceStore::persist_due_occurrences_page.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent codex review reported no actionable correctness findings, the substantive automated review completed without actionable comments, and the exact one-commit head passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Reused occurrence-page serialization and retained all selection and transaction policy in the kernel. Reran the complete repository quality gate after the exact implementation state was ready.

outcome.summary: Operators can persist one bounded due recurrence page atomically through deterministic JSON without the CLI inventing clock, catch-up, identity, or execution policy.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0185-atomic-due-recurrence-persistence-cli.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 185 records: 185 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: A writable CLI should preserve the kernel atomic unit rather than loop over exact-coordinate commands.
Validation of simple identity and allocation bounds should happen before storage access; revision and transaction checks belong to the kernel.
Read-only due and writable persist-due output should share one exact page projection.
The command persists provenance only and cannot generate task identities, materialize, dispatch, retry, grant permission, or execute work.
